arguments.content: Pattern: introducing mandatory application receipts in an independently shipped client can convert completed writes into caller-visible failures. A released provider may still apply the mutation and return its legacy success shape; a stricter client then raises after commit. Feature flags do not protect ordinary operations if receipt enforcement is outside the flag. Receipt-bearing mocks can hide this mixed-version failure. Review the actual supported provider source, distinguish persisted state from caller outcome, and keep a compatibility test asserting both. Preserve legacy success until receipt support is established. Observed as P1 in enhanced-settings Task 1: staged client requires applied=True; eval-release provider applies values and returns only ok=True. This is a post-write acknowledgment regression, not evidence that values were lost.
